scope: Line-by-line review of the last-resort pick-resolution layer (scripts/originate.py rungs, scripts/pinnacle_lines.py, scripts/hltv_ranking.py, scripts/c03ef201_research.py, scripts/build_origination.py replay boundary, data/origination/aliases.json) and the runner research workflow, against official and first-party sources. Every item links the evidence used; nothing here is a probability input.
method: Each item was reproduced in the session workspace or on GitHub runner workflow runs 39198880905, 39204191252 and 39204781421 (2026-10-19, 04:19Z-05:29Z) and checked against the linked source pages and APIs. 'fixed' items carry regression tests; 'needs review' items were deliberately left flagged rather than silently decided.

items.finding: Two provider-name joins were needed to research the Stake Ranked Episode 6 closed-qualifier fixtures: HLTV lists 'Betclic vs Spirit Academy' where Hotspawn lists 'Apogee Betclic vs Spirit Academy', and 'Sangal vs Aurora Young Blud' where Hotspawn lists 'Sangal vs Aurora YB'.
items.handling: Added as competition-scoped registry entries ('Betclic' -> 'Apogee Betclic', 'Aurora Young Blud' -> 'Aurora YB', applies_to: Stake Ranked Episode 6: Closed Qualifier only), each with the HLTV match page and the Hotspawn fixture page as evidence. Same documented evidence class as the earlier reviewed WBT join: exact event slot, exact start time, one exact-name opponent. The joins are published and flagged so a human can confirm or reject them; they never apply outside their declared competition.

evidence.detail: HLTV match 2399772 lists 'Betclic vs Spirit Academy' at 2026-10-19T09:00Z — the exact Hotspawn fixture 1082152 slot with the exact opponent name.
Hotspawn fixture 1082152 lists 'Apogee Betclic' in the same event and slot; the event inventory contains no separate 'Betclic' competitor.
HLTV match 2399777 lists 'Sangal vs Aurora Young Blud' at 2026-10-20T12:00Z — the exact Hotspawn fixture 1082157 slot with the exact opponent name.
Both entries carry full evidence links, competition scopes and review notes in the published registry (updated 2026-10-19).

items.finding: scripts/pinnacle_lines.py accepted any two-participant matchup as a series moneyline, so board specials ('Yes'/'No', 'Odd'/'Even') could produce a quote when a caller did not pass team names — observed directly by the c03ef201 deep probe on 2026-10-19 (series_moneyline returned quotes for Yes/No matchups). Separately, price arrays keyed by participantId were assumed to be in participant order.
items.handling: Specials are rejected by participant text before any price is read (regex-tested against Yes/No, Odd/Even, Tie and 'Team By N' grids). Price-to-name mapping prefers participantId keys and realigns the converted decimals onto participant order; ordering fallback applies only when neither price carries a key. Regression tests: tests/test_unresolved_rungs.py (PinnacleSpecialsTest, PinnacleRowsTest). Session be84edde's earlier TWC quotes were unaffected (they always passed explicit team names) and are not restated.

evidence.detail: The _SPECIAL participant guard and _resolve_participants realignment live in the module used by every Pinnacle read.
The public guest board where specials and team series share one matchup list; period 0 is the series line and periods >= 1 repeat per-map prices (session be84edde's dated finding, relied upon here).
Regression tests cover specials rejection, participant-id mapping, ordering fallback and the period-0-only series rule.

items.finding: The first runner probe (2026-10-19T04:21Z) could not read HLTV at all (HTTP 403 with a browser-mimicking User-Agent) and the bare https://www.hltv.org/ranking/ path answered HTTP 404 even with the project UA.
items.handling: The probe now uses the same honest project User-Agent that scripts/sources.py uses (HLTV match and team pages answer 200). The ranking capture reads the canonical https://www.hltv.org/ranking/teams page and dates the model input from HLTV's own publication slug (e.g. /ranking/teams/2026/october/12, confirmed from team-page rank links), never the fetch wall clock.

evidence.detail: Canonical world-ranking page; answered 200 with 245 team rows on the 2026-10-19T05:29Z probe run.
HLTV team page whose World ranking row links the dated publication /ranking/teams/2026/october/12/details/12916 — the authoritative publication date source.
Dated request manifest: run 1 recorded the 403/404 trail; run 2 (2026-10-19T05:22-05:29Z) recorded the successful reads with response hashes.

items.finding: The brief asks for a pick or probability for every Hotspawn match, while the published ladder left low-tier fixtures blank whenever no exchange, sportsbook or rating row existed. Two gaps needed explicit, labelled rungs rather than silent blanks or invented numbers.
items.handling: Two last-resort rungs were added after every existing rung and never override one: (1) the HLTV world-ranking research model — uncalibrated 400-scale logistic transform of HLTV's official weekly ranking points, both teams required on the same dated publication, 14-day ceiling; (2) wide-book indicative guidance — midpoint of the narrowest observed book that every spread ceiling rejected, badged 'Guidance only', excluded from MONEY_METHODS and from the leaderboard plan's upset rules, with an exactly-even midpoint published as no directional pick. Both replay from saved originals at build time (scripts/build_origination.py).

evidence.detail: The HLTV ranking model: inputs link their own ranking page; alias-aware; fail-closed on stale or incomplete publications.
The methodology page publishes both formulas, their order in the ladder and their limits (step 05 plus the two estimation sections).
Tests pin the order: money beats guidance; Valve beats guidance; HLTV ranking beats guidance; a featured model is never downgraded to guidance; guidance never enters MONEY_METHODS.

items.finding: After the new rungs and the two identity joins, 31 of 34 active fixtures carry a researched estimate. Three stay blank: ex-6666–Privateer (1081131), The Last Resort–LFO 10 (1079643), Chinggis Warriors–WXM (1081863).
items.handling: Each blank is intentional under the published rules: one team per fixture (ex-6666, LFO 10, WXM) has an official HLTV team page but no HLTV world-ranking entry, no Valve rating row and no price on any checked provider. The site's executive summary and the complete-list page publish them in the unresolved section with their full research trails and official links; nothing is filled with a guess.

evidence.detail: Official HLTV team page for ex-6666: the team exists (CCT Europe 2026 Series fixtures) but has no World ranking row.
Official HLTV team page for LFO 10: no World ranking row.
Official HLTV team page for WXM: no World ranking row.
The dated research dossier: every stage of every blank fixture with its exact failure reason and source URL.

items.finding: 1xbet.com's public line page answers the GitHub runner with HTTP 203 and a body listing none of the uncovered fixtures. bo3.gg's match pages are a Nuxt client shell; its API rejects the probed candidate paths with {'error': 'Invalid API path'} and the bundled JS chunks expose no match-data API path to the probe. Direct sandbox reads of Hotspawn, HLTV and bookmaker sites remain blocked (documented earlier).
items.handling: Both providers are recorded as dated access observations with saved, hash-checked originals — never as proof of no market. All live research runs on the GitHub runner through .github/workflows/c03ef201-research.yml (dispatch is HTTP 403 for this token, so a push trigger with a report-commit guard is used; the workflow commits only data/research/c03ef201/ and never deploys).

evidence.detail: Per-provider reachability, listing scans and API-path discovery results for the 2026-10-19 runs.
The runner research workflow: read-only provider GETs, reports-only commits, push-trigger guard, never deploys.

items.finding: New sources must be replayable like every existing one: 'Every published probability is replayed from its saved original response before the site is built.'
items.handling: The replay boundary (scripts/pipeline_audit.py + scripts/build_origination.py) learned the new rungs: Pinnacle quotes replay through the saved guest-board capture with per-league request observations; HLTV ranking estimates recompute from the saved official ranking capture; guidance rows re-derive the unique-provider, widest-book-rejected, narrowest-remaining selection and recompute the midpoint from the saved market observations. The full suite (708 tests) and the built-site validator both pass with the extended boundary.

evidence.detail: replay_provider_quote gained the Pinnacle branch with manifest observation checks against the exact straight-market endpoint.
validate_origination replays HLTV-model and guidance rows from their saved originals and rejects any divergence at build time.
